Subject: VPC annex — forensic artifact request & license rollback scope

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're progressing the procurement approval but Legal has two asks before we can finalize the Order Form and annex for the private VPC deployment:

1) License rollback / runbook: they want explicit language describing what is delivered to us in the event of termination — specifically whether a runnable snapshot is provided or just artifacts (DB dump, model weights, proof-of-access).

2) Forensic artifacts / witnessing: because we operate in regulated diagnostics, we need an auditable transfer path for a forensic snapshot and an option for a short witness window to validate the transfer. They're open to a mutually agreeable technical test but want it in writing.

I've attached the current SOW (HealthCo_SOW_v3.pdf) and flagged the relevant procurement notes. Can you loop in Legal/Product and respond with the proposed annex language and a suggested transfer/test procedure? We're on a tight timeline — procurement is hoping to sign by Mar 1.

Also, if there are any commercial implications (credits/limit to liability) please flag them early.

Cheers,
Sam
Sam Wilder
Head of Procurement — HealthCo Medical Systems
security@healthco.com

P.S. We'll want a short call to align on the technical proof-of-transfer; availability Tuesday/Wednesday afternoon PT.

Subject: Re: VPC annex — forensic artifact request & license rollback scope

Folks — I've reviewed the SOW and Priyom's draft. Key points and proposed compromise language below (summary, full redline attached):

Summary of proposed compromise:
- We will commit to delivering forensic artifacts and a supervised transfer of a snapshot that enables HealthCo to verify access to customer data and model outputs for the purpose of continuity. The annex will NOT grant an unrestricted right to operate Redwood's proprietary serving runtime. Instead, the annex will provide a "limited, time-bound, jurisdiction-scoped" runtime bundle sufficient for HealthCo's incident response and continuity testing.
- Definition: "Forensic snapshot" = configuration files, immutable model artifacts, database exports, KV cache dump and a manifest of checksums; "Runnable snapshot" = a packaged environment that can be executed in a validated test harness for a 14-day acceptance window only.
- Acceptance & witnessing: we propose a 4-hour witnessed transfer window during which HealthCo may run pre-agreed integrity checks. Redwood will provide a checksum manifest and logged transfer receipts. Any in-person witnessing will be strictly observation-only — no operator access to Redwood control plane.
- Limitations: Redwood disclaims liability for reconstruction or reconstitution outside the agreed test harness; any productionization beyond the acceptance window requires a separate license and support contract.

Commercial notes:
- If HealthCo requires a runnable snapshot with extended run rights, that is a commercial uplift (we should offer a one-time fee or a monthly support/hosted fallback commitment).
- We can offer a limited credit (to be confirmed with Finance) if timeline constraints drive an additional engineering scope.

I've attached the full redline (redwood_priv_annex_redline.docx) with bracketed language for negotiation. Priyom — please share the redline with Sam and suggest a 30-minute technical sync to walk through the transfer checklist. Ben — confirm if you want me to mark any clauses as non-negotiable for legal review.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_priv_annex_redline.docx (track changes)
